new_scholarship.name: National Humanities Center Residential Fellowship
new_scholarship.degree_levels: PhD (terminal degree required; postdoctoral researchers and doctoral candidates are not eligible)
new_scholarship.program_type: Independent humanities institute research fellowship (private nonprofit)
new_scholarship.duration: Academic year (September-May), or fall semester (September-December) or spring semester (January-May)
new_scholarship.deadline: Applications open July 1; deadline October 1; letters of recommendation due October 8
new_scholarship.application_period: Opens July 1, closes October 1 (letters of recommendation October 8)
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Holders of a PhD or equivalent terminal degree earned at least five years before applying, engaged in humanities research that will result in publication, with a substantial record of peer-reviewed scholarship beyond the dissertation. Faculty at research universities, liberal arts and teaching colleges, HBCUs, HSIs, tribal colleges and universities and international institutions, as well as independent scholars, may apply. Applicants of any citizenship are eligible and the Center sponsors J-1 Research Scholar visas.
coverage: Individually determined stipend (the Center seeks to provide about half of the Fellow's salary)
Round-trip travel to Durham, North Carolina and back for the Fellow and immediate family living with the Fellow
benefits: Private study in the Center's building for the fellowship term
Library and reference support, including procurement of research materials
Breakfast and lunch on weekdays in the Teachers' Commons
Fellowship term in a residential community of humanities researchers
requirements: 1,000-word project proposal
Short bibliography
Brief curriculum vitae (maximum four pages)
One-page tentative outline of the project structure
Three letters of recommendation (due October 8)
application_method: Submit the online application through the Center's application portal
Upload the proposal, bibliography, CV and outline
Provide names and contact details of three references, who are emailed a link to upload their letters
new_scholarship.english_requirement: Fluency in written and spoken English is required.
new_scholarship.selection_notes: Applicants are informed by email in February; the fellowship class is typically announced in early April; all applicants receive final notification by the end of March. Alternates are offered fellowships by telephone.
new_scholarship.best_fit: Mid-career or senior humanities scholars with a published book or substantial peer-reviewed record who need a residential writing term.
new_scholarship.notes: The Center does not fund post-docs, doctoral research, creative writing (fiction or poetry), edited volumes, collections of primary sources, textbooks or projects derivative of a dissertation. Stipends are taxable and are salary replacement only; no indirect costs or fringe benefits are included and institutional overhead is not allowed.
new_scholarship.description: The National Humanities Center, an independent humanities institute in Durham, North Carolina, awards residential fellowships of an academic year or a semester to scholars in advanced humanities research. The stipend is set individually and is intended to cover roughly half of the Fellow's salary, with the home institution covering the remainder, and the Center additionally pays round-trip travel for the Fellow and accompanying immediate family. Applicants of any nationality may apply and the Center sponsors eligible international scholars on J-1 Research Scholar Exchange Visitor visas. Applications for the 2028-29 academic year open on July 1, 2027 with an October 1, 2027 deadline.

programme_detail_official.deadline_central_display: All materials are due October 1, 2027, except for letters of recommendation, which are due October 8.

The page read on 2026-10-04 states the Center 'will begin accepting applications for the 2028-29 academic year on July 1, 2027 with a deadline of October 1, 2027', so the 2027-28 cycle has already closed.
programme_detail_official.status_note: The 2027-28 competition closed on October 1, 2026, three days before this verification. The next published window opens July 1, 2027.
programme_detail_official.funding_duration: Academic year (September-May) or one semester (fall September-December or spring January-May)
programme_detail_official.tuition_coverage_note: The fellowship pays a stipend as salary replacement and pays round-trip travel; it does not fund tuition, and it does not fund research travel, document collections, moving, shipping or living expenses.
programme_detail_official.funding_label: Individually determined stipend, generally about half the Fellow's academic salary, plus round-trip travel to Durham for the Fellow and immediate family; the home institution is expected to cover the remaining salary
benefits: Individually determined stipend, sized to provide about half of the Fellow's salary
Round-trip travel for the Fellow and any immediate family members living with the Fellow in North Carolina
Private study for the fellowship term
Library services and research material procurement
eligibility: Hold a PhD or equivalent terminal degree (such as an MFA) earned at least five years before applying
Be working on a significant project beyond the dissertation, with at least one single-authored book or a substantial body of peer-reviewed scholarship
Be engaged in humanities research that will result in publication
Hold a continuing academic appointment, or be an independent scholar
Not be a postdoctoral researcher; the Center does not fund post-docs
Not be a doctoral candidate; the Center does not fund doctoral research
programme_detail_official.citizenship_residency: No citizenship or residency restriction; the Center welcomes applications from scholars engaged in advanced humanities research regardless of citizenship or national origin and sponsors eligible international applicants on J-1 Research Scholar Exchange Visitor visas.
programme_detail_official.international_eligibility: International scholars are eligible, including accompanying legal spouses and unmarried children under 21 who may be sponsored on J-2 visas. Exchange visitors must satisfy English proficiency and medical insurance requirements.
degree_levels: Terminal degree holders (PhD or equivalent such as MFA)
programme_detail_official.study_mode: Residential, in person at the Center in Durham, North Carolina
programme_detail_official.research_requirement: A specific, well-defined humanities research project, typically a single-authored book, that is not a collection of primary sources, an edited volume, a dissertation derivative, creative writing, a pedagogical work or a policy report.
programme_detail_official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Humanities research, including interdisciplinary work; projects from the natural and social sciences, arts, professions and public life are accepted only where they are informed by and contribute to humanities scholarship.
programme_detail_official.application_method: Complete the online application in the Center's portal and upload all documents; three references are emailed a link to upload their letters separately.
programme_detail_official.application_route: Direct application to the National Humanities Center.
requirements: 1,000-word project proposal describing objectives, significance, sources and methodology, plus current project status and projected timeline
Short bibliography
Curriculum vitae of no more than four pages
One-page tentative outline of the structure of the project, indicating stage of completion
Names and contact information for three references
documents: Project proposal (1,000 words, uploaded to the portal)
Three letters of recommendation (uploaded by referees, due October 8)
programme_detail_official.english_requirement: Fluency in written and spoken English is required.
programme_detail_official.english_requirement_note: Application materials must be submitted through the online portal, which converts uploads to PDF; the Center advises saving files as PDF first because some non-Latin characters may not survive conversion.
selection_criteria: Strength and significance of the project proposal
Stage of completion and feasibility of the plan
programme_detail_official.selection_weighting: NHC Fellows are chosen based on the strength of the project proposal and its supporting documents rather than on the length of the CV; the letter of recommendation should speak to the merits of the project.
programme_detail_official.duration: Academic year (September through May), fall semester (September through December) or spring semester (January through May); partial terms cannot be accommodated.
award_holder_conditions: Resident at the Center for the fellowship term; travel requiring an absence of three or more weekdays must be approved in advance
Long absences of ten or more consecutive days may not be approved
Attend two mandatory orientation sessions and project presentations in the first three weeks, and lunches with the Board of Trustees in October and March
Submit a fellowship evaluation and a summary of scholarly work at the end of the term
Complete a fellowship evaluation and, for former Fellows, a published project before reapplying
supplements_or_initiatives: Dedicated fellowship support for HBCU faculty
Support for UNCF/Mellon Faculty Residency Program participants
Dedicated support for scholars of early modern China, early-career female philosophers and at-risk scholars
programme_detail_official.description: Residential fellowship of the National Humanities Center, an independent nonprofit humanities institute in Durham, North Carolina, for mid-career and senior scholars in all areas of the humanities. The award provides an individually determined stipend intended to cover about half the Fellow's salary and pays round-trip travel to Durham for the Fellow and accompanying immediate family. It is a research and writing award: it does not fund tuition, postdoctoral positions or doctoral research, and it requires full-time residence at the Center.
programme_detail_official.coverage: Stipend of roughly half salary plus round-trip travel; no tuition, research travel, document purchase, moving, shipping or living costs.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you held your PhD or equivalent terminal degree at least five years before the application deadline
Have a published book or a substantial peer-reviewed body of scholarship beyond the dissertation ready to list in the CV
Draft a 1,000-word proposal that states the project's current stage and projected timeline in the final paragraph
Prepare a one-page chapter outline showing the stage of completion of each section
Choose three referees who can speak to the merits of the project, ideally not from your own institution or dissertation committee
Ask your home institution's grants office to confirm it will cover the salary portion the Center will not fund
common_rejection_risks: Projects that are derivative of the applicant's dissertation
Creative writing such as fiction or poetry, which the Center cannot fund
Projects that are collections of primary sources, edited volumes, textbooks or syllabi
Non-humanities work such as white papers or policy reports
Proposals that do not describe the project's current status and projected timeline, which may be deemed ineligible
Insufficiently developed scholarly record beyond the dissertation
Missing letters of recommendation, which makes an application incomplete and ineligible for review
estimated_uncovered_costs: Roughly the remaining half of your academic salary, which the Center expects your home institution to cover
Living expenses in North Carolina, including housing, which Fellows arrange themselves
Research travel beyond the trip to Durham
Primary source document collections, editing costs, moving and shipping
Institutional overhead, indirect costs and fringe benefits, which are not permitted
document_audit: CV within the four-page limit and focused on relevant publications
Tentative outline limited to one page and showing stage of completion
Bibliography complete for the proposed project
Three referees who will upload letters by October 8
All files uploaded as PDF to avoid conversion damage to non-English characters

alerts.message: The project description cannot exceed 1,000 words; the system converts submissions to PDF, so re-check the converted file for the final word count.
With rare exceptions the Center cannot pay full salary, so secure your institution's commitment before applying.
If you are notified as an alternate, you have one week to 10 days from the offer date to accept or decline.

submission_workflow: Start preparing in the spring before the July 1 opening, when references are least busy
Submit the online application on or before October 1
Give referees the contact details immediately so their letters arrive before October 8
Confirm the portal shows the application and all three letters as received; the Center does not chase missing letters
Expect a status email in February and the public class announcement in early April

new_scholarship.name: Benjamin A. Gilman International Scholarship
new_scholarship.program_type: Government scholarship (U.S. Department of State, Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs)
new_scholarship.official_source: Benjamin A. Gilman International Scholarship Program (U.S. Department of State, Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs; administered by the Institute of International Education)
new_scholarship.duration: One academic term, a summer, or an academic year abroad, depending on the programme start date
new_scholarship.deadline: Spring 2027 cycle: applications open mid-January 2027; student deadline February 25, 2027 at 11:59pm Pacific Time; advisor certification deadline March 4, 2027
new_scholarship.application_period: Mid-January 2027 to February 25, 2027 (Spring 2027 cycle, for programmes starting May 1, 2027 to April 30, 2028)
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: U.S. citizen undergraduates enrolled at a two-year or four-year college or university who receive, or will receive during the study abroad term, a Federal Pell Grant. The award supports credit-bearing academic study and career-oriented internships abroad in any field and world region.
benefits: 12 months of noncompetitive eligibility (NCE) hiring status within the U.S. federal government
requirements: Federal Pell Grant eligibility during the application or the study abroad term
Study abroad or internship programme of at least four weeks for the standard Gilman award
Certification of the application by a Study Abroad and Financial Aid Advisor
Statement of purpose and statement of past study abroad participation
At least one academic reference and, for some fields, an additional reference
application_method: Apply online through the Gilman application portal during the open cycle
Have a Study Abroad and Financial Aid Advisor certify the submitted application before the certification deadline
Submit required statements and reference requests as part of the online application
new_scholarship.english_requirement: Applicants must be able to communicate effectively in the language of the host country; the programme requires demonstrated proficiency appropriate to the programme of study abroad.
new_scholarship.selection_notes: Applications are screened for eligibility, reviewed by selection panelists and recommended awards are approved by the U.S. Department of State. Advisors see award status in the advisor account; all applicants are notified by email in the cycle's stated month.
new_scholarship.best_fit: Pell-Grant-receiving U.S. undergraduates needing help defraying the cost of a credit-bearing study abroad programme or internship.
new_scholarship.funding_period: per award (one-time, up to the stated maximum)
new_scholarship.notes: The award is not a full funding package: it is applied to eligible programme costs and does not cover the entire cost of study abroad. The Fall 2026 cycle closed on October 1, 2026, so the next applicable cycle is Spring 2027.
new_scholarship.description: The Benjamin A. Gilman International Scholarship is a congressionally funded programme of the U.S. Department of State's Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs, administered by the Institute of International Education, that awards up to $5,000 to Pell-Grant-receiving U.S. undergraduates for credit-bearing study abroad and career-oriented internships. The award may be used to defray programme tuition, room and board, books, local transportation, insurance, international airfare, passport and visa fees. Recipients also receive 12 months of noncompetitive eligibility for certain U.S. federal jobs. Applications for the Spring 2027 cycle open in mid-January 2027 with a February 25, 2027 deadline.

programme_detail_official.application_cycle: Spring 2027 cycle; applications open mid-January 2027, for programmes starting May 1, 2027 to April 30, 2028
programme_detail_official.deadline_central_display: The application deadline is Thursday, February 25, 2027, at 11:59pm Pacific Time, and the advisor certification deadline is Thursday, March 4, 2027.
programme_detail_official.deadline_note: The Fall 2026 cycle closed on October 1, 2026 (certification October 8, 2026) and is no longer applicable. The Fall 2026 cycle encompassed Winter/January 2027 through academic year 2027-2028 programmes; the Spring 2027 cycle is the next open window, opening mid-January 2027 with the same eligible programme start range.
programme_detail_official.status_note: The published next window is the Spring 2027 application, opening mid-January 2027 with a February 25, 2027 student deadline and March 4, 2027 advisor certification deadline; all applicants are notified in May 2027.
programme_detail_official.funding_duration: One academic term, summer or academic year abroad
programme_detail_official.tuition_coverage_note: Award recipients 'must use the award to defray eligible study or intern abroad costs', and programme tuition is listed first among those eligible costs; the award is up to $5,000 and is not stated to cover tuition in full.
programme_detail_official.funding_label: Up to $5,000 merit-based award applied to eligible study abroad costs (tuition, room and board, books, local transport, insurance, airfare, passport and visa fees), plus 12 months of federal noncompetitive eligibility; not full funding
benefits: 12 months of noncompetitive eligibility (NCE) hiring status within the U.S. federal government
Access to a nationwide network of Gilman Scholars and alumni
eligibility: Enrolled in a two-year or four-year college or university as an undergraduate
Receiving a Federal Pell Grant at the time of application, or able to show the Pell Grant will be received during the study abroad term
Participating in a credit-bearing academic study abroad programme or career-oriented internship abroad
Programme must meet the minimum length and academic-credit requirements of the relevant cycle
programme_detail_official.citizenship_residency: U.S. citizens only; the programme funds American undergraduates studying abroad.
programme_detail_official.international_eligibility: Not applicable as a grant to non-U.S. citizens; the award is for U.S. citizen undergraduates, regardless of the destination country, which may be in any world region.
programme_detail_official.study_mode: Credit-bearing academic study abroad or career-oriented internship abroad
programme_detail_official.research_requirement: No research proposal is required; academic coursework and, for internships, career-oriented placement is funded in any field.
programme_detail_official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All academic fields, all world regions and all U.S. states are eligible; separate supplemental funding exists for STEM coursework and for critical-need languages.
programme_detail_official.application_method: Submit the online application in the Gilman portal during the open cycle, then have a Study Abroad and Financial Aid Advisor certify it before the certification deadline.
programme_detail_official.application_route: Direct online application to the Gilman Programme, with institutional advisor certification.
requirements: Federal Pell Grant eligibility
Admission to or enrolment in a credit-bearing study abroad or internship programme of qualifying length
Advisor certification of the application
Statement of purpose
Statement of past study abroad participation
Academic reference (and additional references in some fields)
documents: Study abroad programme acceptance or enrolment documentation
Statement of past study abroad participation
programme_detail_official.english_requirement: Applicants must be able to study or intern in the language of the destination; proficiency appropriate to the programme is expected.
programme_detail_official.english_requirement_note: The programme is open to all fields and destinations, so the language requirement follows the host programme rather than a single programme-wide test score.
selection_criteria: Demonstrated financial need through Pell Grant eligibility
Academic merit and quality of the proposed study abroad or internship programme
Quality of the applicant essays and recommendations
Adherence to programme and submission requirements
programme_detail_official.selection_weighting: Applications pass an eligibility screen, are reviewed by selection panelists, and recommended awards are approved by the U.S. Department of State; weights for individual criteria are not published.
programme_detail_official.duration: Varies by term: spring, summer, fall, winter or academic year, matched to the programme start date
award_holder_conditions: Award must be used only for eligible study abroad or internship costs
Applications must be certified by a Study Abroad and Financial Aid Advisor
Programme start date must fall inside the eligible range for the cycle applied for
supplements_or_initiatives: STEM Supplemental Award for STEM coursework or internships abroad
Critical Need Language Award for languages important to U.S. national security
Gilman-McCain Scholarship for veterans and their family members
Gilman Skills for America Scholarship for two-year college students, with up to $5,000 and no minimum programme length
programme_detail_official.description: A congressionally funded programme of the U.S. Department of State's Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs, administered by the Institute of International Education since 2001, awarding up to $5,000 to Pell-Grant-receiving U.S. undergraduates for credit-bearing study abroad and career-oriented internships. Nearly 3,000 awards are made each academic year, and 72% of scholars come from small towns or rural communities. Award recipients may defray programme tuition, room and board, books, local transportation, insurance, international airfare, passport and visa fees, and they gain 12 months of federal noncompetitive eligibility.
programme_detail_official.coverage: Up to $5,000 usable against programme tuition, room and board, books, local transportation, insurance, international airfare, passport and visa fees; no living-cost or full-tuition guarantee.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are a U.S. citizen enrolled as an undergraduate at a two-year or four-year institution
Document your Federal Pell Grant status for the application year or the study abroad term
Match your programme start date to the correct cycle: Spring 2027 covers programmes starting May 1, 2027 to April 30, 2028
Meet with your Study Abroad and Financial Aid Advisor early, because certification closes March 4, 2027
Draft the statement of purpose and the statement of past study abroad participation
common_rejection_risks: Missing or late advisor certification, which invalidates an otherwise complete application
Applying in the wrong cycle for the programme start date
Not receiving or not able to demonstrate Federal Pell Grant eligibility
Submitting after the 11:59pm Pacific Time deadline, which is firm and not extended
Proposals or internships that are not credit-bearing or not career-oriented
Missing the programme minimum length requirement for the standard award
estimated_uncovered_costs: Most of the total cost of study abroad, since the award is capped at $5,000
Any programme cost not on the eligible list
Costs for a term or programme length not covered by the cycle applied for
Living costs beyond room and board already charged by the programme
document_audit: Pell Grant verification for the correct academic year
Study abroad or internship programme details with confirmed start date
Statement of past study abroad participation
Reference submissions received before the deadline

submission_workflow: Apply for admission to a qualifying study abroad or internship programme early enough to have documentation before mid-January 2027

Submit the application by February 25, 2027 at 11:59pm Pacific Time
Send your advisor the certification request immediately and confirm certification before March 4, 2027
Watch for the award notification email in May 2027
